Impaired Glucose Tolerance
Impaired Glucose Tolerance is a condition indicating elevated blood sugar levels, but not yet at the threshold of diabetes. It can progress to Type 2 Diabetes if lifestyle factors are not improved.

Gestational Diabetes (GDM)

People with Type 2 diabetes benefit from exercise for weight management and insulin efficiency, reducing the risk of complications such as eye, kidney, and heart diseases.<SEP>Type 2 Diabetes refers to a chronic condition characterized by high blood glucose levels due to insulin resistance or deficiency and often requires lifestyle changes and medication for management.<SEP>Type 2 diabetes is a specific form of diabetes where the body does not produce enough insulin or cannot effectively use the insulin it makes, often associated with lifestyle factors.

Pre-diabetes

It is important for people with diabetes to be aware of this risk."<<关系描述>>"Description not available in text.<SEP>Hypoglycaemia is the condition of having low blood sugar levels, which can cause symptoms such as tiredness and confusion, and poses a risk of severe complications if not treated promptly.

Hyperglycaemia
Hyperglycaemia is when blood glucose levels rise too high, potentially leading to the production of ketones and conditions like ketoacidosis in people with Type 1 diabetes.

Long Term Complications of Diabetes
Long term complications arise from consistently high blood glucose levels over time, leading to damage in blood vessels and increased risk for heart disease, kidney failure, eye problems, nerve issues, infections, and lower limb amputations.

Oral Medication

data.entity_name: Routine Blood or Urine Glucose Test
data.content:
Routine Blood or Urine Glucose Test
Routine blood or urine glucose tests are standard medical procedures used to screen for diabetes or monitor its progression by measuring blood sugar levels.

Insulin Resistance
Insulin resistance is a condition where the body's cells do not respond properly to insulin, leading to high blood sugar levels and often progressing to Type 2 Diabetes.

Healthy Diet
A healthy diet involves consuming a balanced and nutritious meal plan that is crucial for managing Type 2 Diabetes. It helps in controlling blood sugar levels and overall health.

Ketone Strips
Ketone strips are test strips used to detect the presence of ketones in urine. They help monitor for ketoacidosis, a serious complication in people with Type 1 Diabetes or severe cases of Type 2 Diabetes.

Healthcare Professional
A healthcare professional is a medical practitioner who provides advice and support to people with diabetes. They help in managing the condition through various means including medication, lifestyle changes, and regular check-ups.

Physical Activity
Physical activity is any bodily movement produced by the contraction of skeletal muscles that increases energy expenditure. Regular physical activity can help manage Type 2 Diabetes by improving insulin sensitivity and blood glucose levels.<SEP>Physical activity refers to any form of exercise or movement that helps improve heart health, blood glucose control, cholesterol levels, and overall quality of life.

Nausea and Vomiting
Nausea and vomiting are symptoms that can occur as a result of high blood glucose levels. They may indicate the presence of hyperglycaemia or other complications.

Ketoacidosis (Type 1 Diabetes)
Ketoacidosis is a serious condition in which high levels of ketones accumulate in the bloodstream. It commonly occurs in people with Type 1 Diabetes when there is insufficient insulin.

Lower Limb Amputations
Lower limb amputations are a severe long-term complication of diabetes that can occur due to poor blood circulation and nerve damage. Effective management is crucial to prevent this.

Portion Sizes
Controlling portion sizes is an important aspect of healthy eating, especially for people with diabetes.<SEP>Portion sizes for vegetables can vary based on availability but should be generous when a variety is not available.

Blood Vessel Damage
Damage to blood vessels is a common long-term complication of diabetes that can affect the heart, eyes, kidneys, and nerves. Managing glucose levels helps prevent this.

Blood Sugar Levels
Blood Sugar Levels refer to the concentration of glucose in the bloodstream, which is a key indicator for diagnosing and managing diabetes. These levels can be assessed via routine tests or glucose tolerance tests and are closely monitored in individuals with diabetes, as they can be influenced by carbohydrate intake. Maintaining stable blood sugar levels through diet is crucial for overall health; foods such as legumes, sweet potato, oats, and oat bran, which have a low glycaemic index (GI), provide slower-releasing energy and help manage these levels effectively.

Carbohydrates
Carbohydrates are a type of nutrient that have the biggest effect on blood sugar levels and should be managed carefully by people with diabetes.

Starches
Starches include bread, pasta, rice, pap and starchy vegetables like potatoes and butternut. They are part of the carbohydrate group.<SEP>Starchy foods like rice or potatoes are mentioned as common side dish options but recommend choosing healthier alternatives.

Sugars
Sugar is a type of carbohydrate found in sweets, chocolates, cakes, treats, cold drinks, and other refined products. It should be consumed in controlled quantities by people with diabetes.

Dairy
Dairy foods can contain natural sugars and should be eaten in controlled portions to manage blood sugar levels.

Fruits
Fresh fruits are recommended for their nutritional value and help in managing blood sugar levels compared to processed snacks."<<关系描述>>"Nutritional value, blood sugar management<SEP>Fruits are a type of food that contains natural sugars and should be part of the diet for people with diabetes, but consumed in appropriate quantities.<SEP>Fruits contain natural sugars which can affect blood sugar levels but do not provide detailed information on their nutritional value or energy content.

Nuts
Eating nuts is encouraged for their nutritional value but should be done in appropriate portions.

Unsweetened Dairy Products
Unsweetened dairy products are recommended as a healthier alternative to sweetened ones, especially for people with diabetes.

Good Choices
Making good choices involves selecting nutritious foods like fruits, vegetables, nuts, and unsweetened dairy over less healthy options.

Family, Friends, Colleagues
Family, friends, and colleagues can provide support during the start of a new exercise program.

Nutritional Value
Eating a variety of foods high in nutritional value is important for overall health and managing blood sugar levels.

Aerobic Exercises
Aerobic exercises include activities like running, cycling, or brisk walking. They are recommended to be combined with resistance training in an exercise program.

Well-fitting Footwear
Well-fitting footwear is important for maintaining foot health, especially during exercise.

Resistance Training
Resistance training includes weightlifting and bodyweight exercises such as push-ups. It is part of a balanced exercise regimen for managing diabetes.

Exercise Program
Starting a new exercise program can help manage Type 2 diabetes through weight loss and improved insulin utilization.

Blood Pressure Reduction
Regular exercise helps lower blood pressure, beneficial for people with diabetes to reduce the risk of complications.

Activity Diary
Keeping an activity diary helps stay motivated during an exercise program.

Heart Disease Risk
Smoking can accelerate the small blood vessel damage in people with diabetes, increasing their risk of heart diseases.

Second-hand Smoke
People exposed to second-hand smoke have a higher risk of heart disease and premature death, especially those with diabetes.

Lifestyle Changes
Making lifestyle changes such as diet and exercise are the most effective ways to prevent and manage lifestyle diseases like diabetes and heart disease.

Quit Smoking
Quitting smoking is crucial for people diagnosed with diabetes to reduce cardiovascular risks.

Smoking
Smoking is not recommended for people with diabetes as it increases the risk of heart disease and other complications.

Home Blood Sugar Monitor
Home blood sugar monitors allow individuals to track their glucose levels and manage diabetes more effectively.

HbA1c Blood Test
An HbA1c test provides an overall picture of average blood sugar levels over a three-month period, guiding healthcare professionals in managing diabetes.

Diabetes Medications
Diabetes medications help lower blood glucose levels, but should be taken in combination with a healthy diet and regular exercise.

Nonstarchy Vegetables
Nonstarchy vegetables are low in energy but high in nutritional value, rich in vitamins, minerals, and fibre. They do not lead to weight gain when prepared healthily.

Vegetables
Vegetables are a category of plant-based food items like mushrooms, aubergine, baby marrow, among others.<SEP>Vegetables play a crucial role in maintaining a balanced diet, particularly when managing carbohydrate intake for those on a low-carb regimen or seeking to fill their plates with nutrient-rich options. The recommended vegetables include a diverse range such as baby marrows, beetroot, brinjal, broccoli, cabbage, carrots, cauliflower, celery, cucumber, green beans, lettuce, marogo, mushrooms, onions, peppers, spinach, and tomatoes. These non-starchy vegetables are low in carbohydrates but rich in vitamins and fibre, making them suitable for managing carb intake while providing essential nutrients. It is important to note that some vegetables can contain natural sugars, which should be managed as part of overall carbohydrate consumption. To achieve a balanced diet, portion control is advised along with the inclusion of interesting and flavorful vegetable options such as salads and other interesting combinations in meals.

Starch
A general term for any kind of carbohydrate that can be used to fill up a plate and provide a balanced meal.<SEP>Starch is a carbohydrate-rich food group important for energy and digestion but can significantly affect blood glucose levels.<SEP>Starchy foods include bread, brown rice, lentils, pap, pasta, porridge, rotis, samp, and wholegrain cereal. Proteins
Proteins provide essential amino acids for muscle repair and growth but their portion size should be managed with other food groups.

Fats
Healthy fats are important, but their portion sizes need to be controlled as part of a balanced diet.<SEP>Healthy fats from nuts, avocado, olives, seeds, and oily fish can provide energy and help absorb fat-soluble vitamins.

Healthy Fats
Healthy fats are important sources of energy for the body and necessary to absorb fat-soluble vitamins. They should be chosen from nuts, avocado, olives, seeds, and oily fish.

Protein Portion Size
The recommended protein portion size is the size of the palm of your hand or a quarter of the plate, including choices like meat, fish, chicken and turkey, eggs, beans, lentils, soya, and cheese.

Starchy-Vegetables
Starchy-vegetables include butternut, mealies, potatoes, and sweet potatoes. They are also high in carbs and should be eaten in moderation.

Food labels may indicate whether food is low GI or not, aiding in making better food choices for maintaining stable blood sugar levels.<SEP>Food labels provide information about the content of food products including nutrition facts and ingredient lists.

Low GI Foods
Low GI foods release energy more controlled and sustainably into the bloodstream compared to high GI foods. They include complex and unrefined carbs like wholewheat bread and brown rice, which have a slower rise in blood sugar levels than refined carbs.

Soluble Fibre
Legumes, sweet potato, oats, and oat bran contain soluble fibre which helps keep blood sugar levels stable by releasing energy slowly into the bloodstream.
